$comment: Provenance for the fixture corpus. Formats drift between editor and game releases;
without this, a test failing six months from now is unattributable.
Everything here was scanned for owner/identity fields before committing - these are
plain ship and multitool objects with no Owner block, so no scrubbing was needed.

notes: Every file carries UsesLegacyColours, so all were exported by a build that
includes the 2026-09-18 fix. A pre-fix export (key absent) must be synthesised
by deleting the key; that case is what the absent-flag rule exists for.
5 files are legacy=true, 12 are legacy=false.
Horizon Omega (Original/New) and Alpha Vector (Original/New) are matched pairs:
the same model and class captured twice, once with UsesLegacyColours set and once
without. They were exported from different saves, so their names, cargo and texture
options differ as well - the model is what is held constant, and the flag is what
distinguishes them. They are the sharpest regression test available for the flag
surviving a conversion.
The Wraith exercises NMSE's AlienShip owner-type mapping; Vintage Interceptor
exercises RobotShip. Starborn Phoenix is a DLC model.
No corvettes, so no fixture exercises the Base sidecar yet.
Multitools carry UseLegacyColours (no trailing s) inline on the object itself,
which is why multitool export never lost it the way ship export did.
Keys: Layout, Store, ScreenData, Seed, CustomisationData, Name, IsLarge,
PrimaryMode, SecondaryMode, UseLegacyColours, Resource.
Six models are covered by their own scene file - three staffs, the swarm tool,
the retro tool and the switch tool - and six share MULTITOOL.SCENE.MBIN and so
can only be told apart by their stats. See MultitoolStatRanges.
Of those six shared-model tools, five have mining of exactly zero and land in
Rifle C: two have no rolled stats at all, and three (Rezosu Z65, Artios-VI,
Vetric-LX) have real rolls of 1.5 to 4.9 damage. All five carry IsLarge=false,
so the body flag and the stat ranges disagree about every one of them.
The two Starbound v0.27 files are byte-identical apart from PrimaryMode and
SecondaryMode, which is which weapon mode was selected when each was exported.

sets.shape: bare pet object with PetAccessoryCustomisation spliced in flat
notes: Carries a SenderData block - LID, UID, USN, PTK - which is where a gifted
creature records who sent it. Every field is empty in this file, so there was
nothing to scrub, but anything added later must be checked: see the note at the
top of this manifest.
CreatureType and Biome are plain words in the payload (Passive, Lush), so the
two things anyone browses creatures by need no database at all.
SpeciesSeed and GenusSeed are plain hex strings, not the [occupied, hex] pair
every other seed in the game uses.
PetBattlerCoreStatClassOverrides holds three inventory classes but
PetBattlerUseCoreStatClassOverrides is false, so they are not in effect - the
real battle classes are procedural and are not derived anywhere yet.

stillNeeded: NMS Companion (Kaii) .shp / .mlt / .cmp / .flt, with and without thumbnails
An NMSE corvette .nmsship, to exercise the Base sidecar
An export with a non-ASCII name, to settle openQuestions.encoding
An NMS Model IO Tool .nmsship ZIP, to validate PK-magic disambiguation

encoding: NMSE writes exports with File.WriteAllText (UTF-8) over a string that already holds
UTF-8 bytes in Latin-1 chars, so non-ASCII is double-encoded on disk. Every fixture
here is pure ASCII, where both readings agree, so the corpus cannot settle whether
NMS-Vault should emit bug-compatible or standards-correct bytes.
